title: WORM-attested admin event handoff playbook and retention automator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem:
Redwood must produce tamper-evident audit evidence for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes that: (1) is region-aware for residency requirements, (2) enforces retention/WORM semantics, and (3) can be handed off to legal/forensics tooling as a verifiable package. Current audit exports are plain logs and periodic snapshots; we lack a reproducible attestation bundle and an automated retention-lift workflow that meets enterprise audit needs.

Proposal summary:
Implement a WORM-attested event handoff playbook and a retention-automation orchestrator. The system will: (a) generate hourly Merkle bundles of admin events per residency boundary, (b) produce a signed attestation manifest (manifest v0.2) that includes per-file digests, region tags, and policy version, (c) write event bundles to object storage with S3 Object Lock configured (governance mode) and an immutable manifest signed by an HSM-backed key, (d) periodically anchor manifest digests to an internal notary service (and optional public ledger for long-term proof), and (e) provide an automated retention-lift workflow requiring multi-approver authorization and audit trail.

Design details:
- Event collection: subscribe to audit event stream (admin actions, config changes, role grants, privileged access sessions). Events are routed by region tag at emit-time.
- Bundle and Merkleization: every hour per-region, build a compact event bundle (newline-delimited protobuf) and compute a Merkle root. Include sequence metadata and epoch timestamp.
- Attestation manifest: JSON lines manifest with: bundle filename, SHA-256 digest, byte-range map, region tag, policy_id, retention_expires, evidence_id. Manifest is signed with HSM private key and includes HSM signature metadata (key_id, sig_algo, timestamp).
- Storage: write bundles+manifests to S3 buckets with Object Lock: mode=GOVERNANCE, retention period populated from retention_expires. For private deployments where S3 is not available, map to on-prem WORM target (tape/object-store) with equivalent retention enforcement and a custody-record in KMS.
- Notarization: publish manifest digest to internal notary service which issues a notarization receipt; optionally mirror digest to an external anchor (e.g., timestamping service) for additional non-repudiation.
- Retention lift: implement an orchestrator service that creates a retention-lift request tied to evidence_id; requires: requestor, purpose, legal_approval_flag, Ops approval (2-of-3) before issuing a nonce to KMS to update governance lock via a time-limited exception. All steps produce auditable events recorded back into system.
- Export & Evidence package: one-click export in Console/Playbook: fetch bundle(s) + manifest + notarization receipts + access logs -> produce a zipped evidence package with an evidence README and verification script that validates signatures and Merkle proofs.

Migration & Backfill:
- Backfill: for last 90 days create retroactive Merkle manifests by streaming existing logs; flag backfilled bundles as such. Where object-store immutability cannot be retroactive (legacy buckets), produce signed manifests and notarization receipts and mark custody as 'best-effort'.

Operational concerns:
- Performance: bundling runs off the critical path; use async workers and prioritized retries for failed writes.
- Cost: extra storage for manifests and notarization receipts; optional external-anchoring is billable.
- Failure modes: split-brain during region failover requires deterministic re-run of bundle generation; manifest schema includes bundle sequence to detect duplicates.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha (internal): implement per-region bundle + manifest + S3 Object Lock write (us-east-1 only). Console: basic export CLI. 2 weeks.
2) Beta (select customers): enable governance-mode object lock + notarization receipts, add retention-lift UI with manual gating. 4 weeks.
3) GA: full region coverage, automated retention-lift with multi-approver, on-prem adaptor, and evidence package tooling. 6 weeks.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a generated hourly bundle: manifest exists, HSM signature verifies, S3 Object Lock retention metadata set and non-overridable by a single user.
- Evidence package produced by Console verifies locally via provided script (digest checks and signature verification).
- Retention-lift requests require at least two independent approvers (legal+ops) and generate a permanent audit trail.
- Backfill for 90-day window produces manifests for >= 95% of days per-region (exceptions logged).

Metrics to track:
- time-to-write-bundle (p95), manifest-sign-time (p95), notarization-latency (p99), export-duration (p95), retention-lift turnaround time, failed-bundle-rate.

Risks & mitigations:
- HSM key compromise: use key rotation & immediate revocation; create cross-signed receipts to allow forensic validation of pre-rotation evidence.
- Customer legal holds overriding retention: implement legal_hold flag that supersedes retention_expiration at policy level and prevent auto-deletion.
- On-prem variance: provide clear contracts describing guarantees for on-prem WORM mapping and include a custody-handoff checklist.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- ENG: event-router changes to ensure region tag propagation (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/12548).
- ENG: bundling worker + Merkle library + manifest producer (prototype branch: feature/eng/merkle-bundles).
- ENG: HSM integration & signature flow (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/keysvc/pull/412).
- ENG: storage writer with Object Lock configuration + on-prem adapter (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/storage/pull/2897).
- UX: Console export flow and retention-lift UI (spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/WORM+Attested+Export+Spec).
- QA: property tests for bundle determinism and verification scripts.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/WORM+Attested+Event+Handoff
- Prototype verification script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/tree/main/evidence-verifier
